items.item_text: J.D. degree and California State Bar member in good standing.
Demonstrated experience handling a wide range of matters in immigration court, including representation in a substantial number of bond hearings, master calendar hearings, and merits hearings;
Minimum of 5-8 years of experience representing detained immigrants in removal proceedings;
Knowledge and experience filing habeas petitions;
Demonstrated experience handling a removal defense docket (including detained and non-detained) of approximately 25-30 cases, including ability to develop and lead case strategy;
Experience in complex motions practice, including Motions to Reopen and Motions to Suppress;
Experience filing and briefing BIA appeals and/or federal court litigation;
Experience working with students and immigrant community organizations and providing trauma-informed client services.

The UC Immigration Legal Services Center (UCIMM) is a university-based, immigration legal services program headquartered at the UC Davis School of Law with staff present and providing legal services at all UC campuses. We provide advice and counsel and direct legal representation in immigration matters, and engage in education and outreach, advocacy, and other strategic initiatives. We offer free services to enrolled undocumented and other immigrant UC students, including U.S. citizens in mixed status families; UC staff and faculty, and low-income immediate family members of enrolled UC students, and some alumni.

Under general direction of the Executive Director, this attorney will be responsible for leading and building the UC Center’s Removal Defense practice, with a focus on representation before the Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR) in both detained and non-detained cases, as well as filing appeals before the Board of Immigration Appeals (BIA) and petitions for review before the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals. This includes bond hearings, master calendar hearings, motions practice, and individual merits hearings. The attorney will prepare and file applications for relief from removal, including Asylum/Withholding of Removal and protection under the Convention Against Torture (CAT), Cancellation of Removal, Adjustment of Status in proceedings, and other forms of relief available in immigration court. Depending on capacity and need, this attorney may also be assigned cases before U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), including Special Immigrant Juvenile Status (SIJS), U Non-Immigrant Visas, and Family-Based Petitions, among others.

An attorney in this role will be expected to be the first responder at the UC Center in removal defense. This includes travel to immigrant detention centers across California, and other locales as part of comprehensive representation before EOIR and other agencies, as necessary. Travel to various UC campuses for client or team meetings, including UC Davis, will also be expected.

This attorney will supervise and mentor attorneys and other staff on removal defense cases as part of building the UC Center’s overall removal defense capacity. Their work in this area will require collaboration with various team members, overseeing case preparation and workflow, maintaining organization, accuracy, and compliance across assigned matters, and ensuring efficient case management and strong client service. The attorney will be expected to closely follow changes to law, policy, and practice before EOIR.

Additionally, this attorney will be expected to assist in our growing Federal Litigation practice, particularly habeas petitions, and any other litigation that may intersect with removal defense before EOIR.
Must be fully fluent in Spanish.
Ability to manage litigation matters with minimal supervision;

Highly organized with strong attention to detail and demonstrated ability to meet deadlines and move work forward; flexible, innovative, able to quickly adapt to changing program needs, and highly-motivated.
Demonstrated ability or willingness to mentor and supervise junior staff;
